title: Break the Big Goal Into Seasons
description: Long goals feel lighter when they are divided into seasons, each with its own smaller finish line.

body.heading: A year is too big to hold
paragraphs: “Learn an instrument this year” or “write a novel” stretches so far ahead that today's practice feels pointless. The distance between effort and result is simply too wide for motivation to cross daily.
Seasons fix the distance. A season is six to ten weeks — long enough to make real progress, short enough that the finish line stays visible from the start.

body.heading: One season, one focus
paragraphs: Give each season a single clear outcome: this season is for scales and three simple songs; next season can worry about performing. At the end of a season, rest briefly, look at what changed, and choose the next focus with fresh information.
Seasons also give you permission to stop. A goal you review four times a year can be adjusted or even retired honestly, instead of quietly abandoned in February.

takeaway: Think in seasons, and big goals become a series of finishable stretches.
